paths.title: Choose a route
paths.description: Routes pick games and settings for different ages and interests. They are optional, can be changed any time, and never limit what you can play.

kids.intro: Picture memory, simple logic and spotting games with short instructions and no rush. Start at level 1 and move up when it feels easy.

goals.1: Play with memory, patterns and logic
goals.3: Clear, friendly feedback after every answer

notes.1: No names, emails or personal details are asked. Progress stays on this device.
notes.2: There are no public rankings or chats.
notes.3: If this site is ever offered to children publicly, parental consent and data rules apply first (see docs/privacy.md).

teens.intro: Harder visual puzzles, strategy problems and working-memory challenges. Beat your own records — there are no public leaderboards.

goals.1: Take on logic and strategy puzzles
goals.2: Push working memory and pattern finding
goals.3: Track personal bests level by level

notes.1: Records are personal and stay on this device.

adults.intro: Practise remembering lists and numbers, staying focused, switching between tasks and planning ahead, in sessions of 3 to 15 minutes.

goals.3: Fit practice into short daily sessions

notes.1: Results describe your performance in these activities only; they are not a medical or psychological evaluation.

seniors.tagline: Clear, calm activities at your own pace.
seniors.intro: Larger text, bigger buttons and no time limits by default. Instructions can be reopened at any moment during a game.

goals.1: Keep a regular routine of mental activity
goals.2: Practise memory and attention at a comfortable pace
goals.3: See your own results over time

notes.1: Choosing this route turns on larger text, comfortable controls and relaxed timing. Change them any time in Settings.
notes.2: A slow or mistaken answer is simply part of practising; it says nothing about your health.

programmers.tagline: Logic, code reading and working memory.
programmers.intro: Trace algorithms, hunt bugs, track variables and reason about dependencies, plus general logic and memory games. Pair it with the programming logic course.

goals.2: Hold program state in working memory
goals.3: Reason about conditions, loops and dependencies

notes.1: Choosing this route opens every level (free play). Turn it off in Settings.
